SeasonResetRequest.description: Which season closes, and what opens after it.

seasonId.description: The season being closed. Naming it rather than saying "the current one" is what makes a retry safe: a second call for a season that already closed is a no-op rather than a second rollover.

archivedEntries.description: How many entries were archived out of the live board.

SubmitScoreRequest.description: One player's score on a board.

playerId.description: Player UUID, Mojang format with dashes.

score.description: The value to submit. How it combines with the stored score is `mode`.

mode.description: REPLACE overwrites, ACCUMULATE adds, MAX keeps the higher of the two. Required — there is no safe default, since each mode is the wrong answer for the other two kinds of board.

seasonId.description: Pin to a season. Omitted means the board's active season.

idempotencyKey.description: Deduplication token. The same key within the service's idempotency window returns the earlier outcome instead of submitting again, so a retry cannot double-count.

effectiveScore.description: The player's score once the mode was applied.

rank.description: 1-indexed rank after the update. 0 when not on the board.

seasonId.description: The season the submission was attributed to.

deduplicated.description: True when the idempotency key matched an earlier submit and nothing changed.

TopResponse.description: The top of a board for one season.

seasonId.description: The season these entries belong to.

bearerAuth.description: The projected ServiceAccount token from /var/run/secrets/grounds/token, with the grounds-services audience.

info.description:
Persistent player rankings. A board is a (boardId, seasonId) pair: the board id is stable per gamemode (`bedwars.solos`), the season rolls over on ops's schedule and the scores from the closed season are archived rather than deleted.

Scores are submitted by whoever owns the result — service-match after a rated match, not the gamemode — and read by anything that renders a board. A submission says how it combines with what is stored: overwrite, add, or keep the better of the two.

A retried submission is the hazard this API is shaped around: a double-counted score is visible to players and stays wrong for a season. Send an idempotency key and a retry costs nothing.
